A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TVQ/RTVQ research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification and dense-prediction experiments, quantization-error measurements, sensitivity studies and loss-landscape analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds GLUE experiments and comparisons with prior task-vector compression methods.

M1.justification: The core TVQ/RTVQ procedures and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. Section 5.3 adds a hybrid application that quantizes TSV-C's singular components, changing the representation being quantized without revising the core algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 extends evaluation beyond vision to eight GLUE language tasks: CoLA, SST-2, MRPC, STS-B, QQP, MNLI, QNLI and RTE. The existing image-classification and NYUv2 coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Table 6 introduces direct compression comparisons with TALL Mask and TSV-C, including TSV-C plus quantization. Figure 11 adds evaluated DARE and TWIN merging methods. These expand the comparison scope beyond v1's retained vision comparator sets.

E3.justification: Added experiments use RoBERTa-base, GLUE-specific Matthews and Pearson/Spearman correlations alongside accuracy, and a TALL-Mask protocol for storage/accuracy comparison. v2 also drops ViT-B/16 from the stated model list, without removing separately reported results. The retained vision experiments preserve their evaluation settings.

E4.justification: Table 6 adds a limited combination analysis comparing TSV-C with and without quantization to test additional compression savings. Existing error-correction, bit-allocation, pruning, similarity and loss-landscape analyses remain unchanged; the enlarged Figure B redisplays the existing similarity analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Parenthesized table values remain differences from FP32 performance, rather than uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Figure 11 adds GLUE performance curves showing near-FP32 performance at 3 bits. New Table 6 reports TVQ at 95.9% and 18.3 Gb, and TSV-C plus TVQ at 95.7% and 11.9 Gb. These are additional comparisons, not improvements over matched v1 results; Tables 1–5 and A–F retain their values.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6 retain the quantization definitions, error bound, base/offset decomposition, bit-allocation assumption and error correction. Neither version adds formal proofs or theorems.

C1.justification: The introduction's contribution statement expands the validated scope to natural language processing, and the conclusion generalizes its task description. The central TVQ/RTVQ contributions, compatibility claims and maximum 92% storage reduction remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations that low-bit quantization generalizes to language tasks and complements SVD compression. Existing explanations involving regularization, pruning, orthogonality and low-bit degradation are retained, without new substantive limitations.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project/code-access link and identifies the released EMR-Merging RoBERTa-base checkpoints in Appendix A.2. Existing vision checkpoint information largely moves from Section 5.1 into that appendix subsection.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for Task Singular Vectors, GLUE, RoBERTa, language datasets and two dense-prediction works. Section 2.1 revises storage-related positioning to discuss TALL Mask and TSV-C's SVD compression, while retaining the broader related-work framing.

P1.justification: Section 5.1 and the conclusion are shortened, Appendix A's dataset descriptions are expanded, and a checkpoint subsection is introduced. Author emails, acknowledgments and a supplementary-material heading are added; the overall narrative structure remains stable.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 6 and Figure 11, enlarges and redraws Figure B with cell values and a task-index key, and relocates several existing displays. Most figures and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The GLUE experiments and direct compression comparisons provide useful support for generality and storage efficiency beyond v1's vision evidence. Added checkpoint/code references and clearer similarity plots improve usability. The gains are bounded by brief descriptions of the new protocols and aggregate NLP reporting; the core method and extensive original evidence remain unchanged.
